pr.title: Inline `FnOnce`/`FnMut`/`Fn` shims once again
pr.description:
This PR fixes the argument checking for `extern "rust-call"` ABI functions with a spread arg, which do no expect their arguments to be exploded from a tuple like closures do.

Secondly, it removes the hack that prevented them from being inlined. This results in more work done by the compiler, but it does end up allowing us to inline functions we didn't before.

Fixes #137901
pr.author: compiler-errors

issues.title: MIR inliner not inlining through `is_some_and` sometimes

processing.reason: The historical wrong transformation is the Inline pass's refusal to inline `extern "rust-call"` callees whose body has `spread_arg.is_some()`. That refusal only leaves a residual shim/function-item call in MIR; it does not change the executed Rust semantics. The regression is a missed optimization (the corrected MIR eventually reaches `_0 = const 64_i32`), and the PR evidence/tests only show CHECK `inlined` versus `CHECK-NOT: inlined`, not different runtime values. The second described error (removing the guard while still requiring a tuple) would be a `bug!`/ICE, not a defined Rust behavior that Miri can execute. Therefore no source-grounded pair of both-valid Rust functions can produce different defined values solely from this historical rewrite.

analysis.summary: The MIR `Inline` pass wrongly handled `extern "rust-call"` callees: it bailed out of inlining any callee with a `spread_arg`, and its argument checker assumed every rust-call argument is exploded from a tuple. The fix allows spread-arg rust-call functions (including FnOnce/FnMut/Fn shims and function items) to inline again while treating a spread arg as a single non-tuple argument; this resolves the missed inlining in #137901.
analysis.originalLogic: In `try_inlining`, when `callsite.fn_sig.abi() == ExternAbi::RustCall`, the pass first rejected user-written rust-call functions with a spread argument: `if callee_body.spread_arg.is_some() { return Err("user-written rust-call functions"); }` (under the comment `FIXME: Don't inline user-written extern "rust-call" functions`). For the remaining rust-call calls it matched `[arg_tuple]` or `[self_arg, arg_tuple]`, then executed `let ty::Tuple(arg_tuple_tys) = *arg_tuple_ty.kind() else { bug!("Closure arguments are not passed as a tuple"); };` and zipped `self_arg_ty.into_iter().chain(arg_tuple_tys).zip(callee_body.args_iter())` to subtype-check each argument. Non-rust-call calls checked arguments in a separate loop. Thus every rust-call callee whose body had `spread_arg.is_some()` was never inlined, leaving shim/function-item calls in MIR.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically wrong transformation was to refuse to inline (return `Err("user-written rust-call functions")`) whenever a rust-call callee has `callee_body.spread_arg.is_some()`, instead of inlining it. This left calls such as `<fn(std::cmp::Ordering) -> bool {std::cmp::Ordering::is_le} as FnOnce<(std::cmp::Ordering,)>>::call_once(...)` as residual calls. A latent second error, avoided by the same patch, is to remove that guard but keep tuple-exploding logic: for a spread-arg callee the caller's single argument is not a tuple, so `let ty::Tuple(...) = *arg_tuple_ty.kind() else { bug!("Closure arguments are not passed as a tuple") }` would hit the `bug!`/ICE (or check the wrong arity and types) rather than treating the spread argument as one argument. The corrected transformation uses `std::slice::from_ref(&arg_tuple_ty)` when `callee_body.spread_arg.is_some()`, otherwise explodes the tuple.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR of functions containing calls whose callee ABI is `extern "rust-call"`: closure calls, `Box<dyn Fn...>`/`dyn FnMut<I>` calls, function-item/fn-pointer calls (`fn() {f}`, `fn() -> i32 {yield_number}`), and user-written `extern "rust-call"` functions with a spread arg. Includes generic rust-call calls (e.g. `call<I: Tuple>(Box<dyn FnMut<I>>, I)`), recursive/cyclic callees, and diverging callees; both `panic=abort` and `panic=unwind`.
analysis.trigger: `callsite.fn_sig.abi() == ExternAbi::RustCall` and either `callee_body.spread_arg.is_some()` (spread-arg user-written rust-call function) or the call's arguments are shaped `[arg_tuple]` / `[self_arg, arg_tuple]`. Spread-arg callees take the single argument directly, whereas closure-style rust-call callees take a tuple that must be exploded.
preconditions: `validate_types` reports no errors for callee/caller bodies.
Callee return type subtypes the destination type via `util::sub_types`.
MIR is available for the callee (shim or user function); intrinsics/virtual instances remain ineligible.
For non-spread rust-call callees the last argument type is `ty::Tuple`; for spread-arg callees it is a single non-tuple type.
pitfalls: Do not assume all rust-call arguments are passed exploded from a tuple; spread-arg callees expect one argument that is not a tuple.
When `spread_arg.is_some()`, build the argument slice with `std::slice::from_ref(&arg_tuple_ty)` so zipping against `callee_body.args_iter()` has correct arity.
Keep the `bug!("Closure arguments are not passed as a tuple")` path reachable only for actual closure/tuple-style rust-call calls, not spread-arg calls.

Removing the no-inline hack permits re-inlining through function-item shims, which can form cycles (`inline_cycle`) and diverging chains (`inline_diverging`); the inliner's cycle/termination handling must cover these.
Generic rust-call calls (`dont_ice_on_generic_rust_call`) previously needed an ICE guard; update `CHECK-NOT: inlined` expectations to `CHECK: (inlined ...)` after enabling inlining.
Test both panic strategies: unwind edges and cleanup blocks differ (`panic-abort` uses `unwind unreachable`, `panic-unwind` uses `unwind continue`/cleanup).
A retained old test name or stale comment does not prove the old no-inline result is correct; compare actual MIR assignments (residual call vs. inlined scope and `const 64_i32`).
analysis.testStrategy: Use MIR-opt tests with `//@ test-mir-pass: Inline` and `// EMIT_MIR <name>.Inline.diff`, plus `//@ compile-flags: --crate-type=lib -C panic=abort` where applicable. Add `// EMIT_MIR_FOR_EACH_PANIC_STRATEGY` to exercise abort and unwind diffs. Build small callers for: (1) a function item passed to `impl FnOnce` (`inline_fn_call_for_fn_def.rs`), (2) `Box<dyn Fn(i32)>` (`inline_box_fn.rs`), (3) generic `Box<dyn FnMut<I>>` with `I: Tuple` (`dont_ice_on_generic_rust_call.rs`, checking no ICE and that `call_mut` inlines), (4) user-written `extern "rust-call"` spread-arg functions, (5) recursive shim calls (`inline_cycle.rs`) and diverging calls (`inline_diverging.rs`). Assert with `// CHECK-LABEL: fn caller(` followed by `// CHECK: (inlined <fn() ... as FnOnce<...>>::call_once - shim(...))` and `// CHECK: (inlined yield_number)` where the callee body becomes `_0 = const 64_i32;`. For the A/B transformation, keep two programs identical except the callee ABI/form: one spread-arg `extern "rust-call"` fn (single non-tuple arg) and one closure/tuple-style callee; verify the spread case inlines without the tuple `bug!`, and verify the closure case still explodes its tuple. Update old `CHECK-NOT: inlined` expectations and use `EMIT_MIR_FOR_EACH_BIT_WIDTH` where pointer-width-dependent MIR differs (issue_59352).
evidence: This PR fixes the argument checking for `extern "rust-call"` ABI functions with a spread arg, which do no expect their arguments to be exploded from a tuple like closures do.
Secondly, it removes the hack that prevented them from being inlined. This results in more work done by the compiler, but it does end up allowing us to inline functions we didn't before.
// CHECK: (inlined <fn() -> i32 {yield_number} as FnOnce<()>>::call_once - shim(fn() -> i32 {yield_number}))
_0 = <fn(std::cmp::Ordering) -> bool {std::cmp::Ordering::is_le} as FnOnce<(std::cmp::Ordering,)>>::call_once(std::cmp::Ordering::is_le, move _5) -> [return: bb2, unwind continue];
calls to trivial functions like `is_le` really ought to MIR-inline, even if done through the voldemort function item like this.

// CHECK: (inlined call_twice::<!, fn() -> ! {sleep}>)
-    // CHECK-NOT: inlined
+    // CHECK: (inlined <fn() -> ! {sleep} as Fn<()>>::call - shim(fn() -> ! {sleep}))
+    // CHECK: (inlined sleep)
